jobs.occupation: Associate researcher in Experimental lung transplantation
jobs.description:
Description of workplaceThe research group is led by Associated professor Sandra Lindstedt and has a long-standing interest in research related to lung transplantation, post-transplant complications, and lung regeneration. The group focuses on developing novel therapeutic strategies to treat lung injury, improve donor organ quality, and reduce complications following lung transplantation. A particular focus is on acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), primary graft dysfunction (PGD), and regenerative approaches to lung repair.
We offerLund University is a governmental authority, which means you get special benefits, generous holidays, and a favorable occupational pension. Read more on the university's website about being employed at Lund University, Work at Lund University
Work descriptionA associate researcher position is available within the Lindstedt research group, focusing on translational research in lung transplantation, lung injury, and regenerative medicine. The duties at the research unit primarily consist of experimental and laboratory-based research, with a particular focus on the development and evaluation of novel therapeutic strategies to improve lung repair and transplantation outcomes.
The main responsibilities include:
independently designing, planning, coordinating, and conducting research projects, as well as collecting, analyzing, interpreting, and managing experimental data.
The work involves the development and optimization of experimental protocols, evaluation of therapeutic interventions, and application of cellular, molecular, ultra-high-plexed immunofluorescence and histological techniques to investigate mechanisms of lung injury, repair, and regeneration.
The position also includes responsibility for preparing high-quality scientific manuscripts for publication in international peer-reviewed journals, contributing to research grant applications, and presenting research findings at national and international scientific conferences.
The majority of the work will be conducted independently, while also involving close collaboration with internal and external research partners and clinical collaborators.
In addition, the position includes mentorship and supervision of doctoral students, Bachelor’s and Master’s students, and other junior researchers, as well as contributing to the coordination and development of ongoing research activities within the group.

Other work tasks might also be included.
QualificationsRequired qualifications
PhD (or equivalent) in biomedical sciences, biotechnology, molecular biology, regenerative medicine, or a related field.
A minimum of four years of documented research experience following completion of the PhD, demonstrating scientific independence and responsibility.
Documented experience in experimental and translational biomedical research, particularly within cell therapies, lung injury, lung transplantation, or regenerative medicine.
Hands-on experience with small and large-animal models and/or ex vivo organ perfusion.
Experience with standard cellular and molecular biology techniques, including cell culture, ELISA, Western blotting, qPCR, immunohistochemistry and high-plexed immunofluorescence.
Demonstrated ability to independently design, plan, coordinate, and conduct complex experimental research projects.
Documented scientific productivity through publications in international peer-reviewed journals.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
Independent and responsible, with the ability to organize and manage research activities and take responsibility for scientific quality and project progress.
Collaborative, with strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively in interdisciplinary research environments.
Analytical and solution-oriented, with the ability to critically evaluate experimental results and address complex scientific challenges.

Meritorious qualifications:
Additional specialized training in experimental transplantation, regenerative medicine, cell therapy, or related disciplines.
Relevant training and certification in laboratory animal science, particularly involving large- and small-animal experimental models.
Completed courses in higher education teaching and pedagogy.
Experience with experimental lung transplantation, including large- and small-animal models of lung injury and transplantation.
Hands-on experience with ex vivo lung perfusion (EVLP) and human ex vivo lung models, including precision-cut lung slices (PCLS).
Experience in the development and evaluation of cell-based and regenerative therapies, particularly mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) and mitochondrial therapeutics.
Experience with cellular, molecular, histological, and proteomic analyses, including the handling and processing of human and animal tissue samples.
Experience in managing and coordinating interdisciplinary research projects and national or international collaborations.
Documented experience in scientific supervision, preparation of research grant applications, and dissemination of research findings through publications and international conferences.

Other information
The position is a fixed-term employment according to the Special Fixed-term Employment (SÄVA) regulations §5 p1 LAS, and it is full-time. The desired start date is 2027-01-01 or as agreed upon, with an end date of 2027-12-31.
How to Apply
Applications are to be submitted via the University’s recruitment system. The application should include a CV and a personal letter justifying your interest in the position and how it matches your qualifications. The application should also include a degree certificate or equivalent and any other document to which you would like to draw attention (copies of grade transcripts, details of referees, letters of recommendation, etc.).

Company Description

Bosch Home Comfort in Tranås develops, manufactures and sells advanced heat pumps that harness energy from nature’s own resources: rock, water and air. Our Tranås site brings together manufacturing, research and development, and business functions, creating an environment where ideas and decisions are closely connected to our products and operations.
We believe in technology that makes a difference: Invented for life.
 

Job Description

Your contribution to something big
Do you enjoy understanding what really drives performance in a manufacturing business, rather than simply reporting the numbers?
As our Plant Controller, you will work at the intersection of finance and manufacturing, partnering closely with Plant Management and colleagues across production, logistics, engineering and other functions.
You will turn financial and operational data into insights that support better decisions, stronger performance and continuous improvement. This is a hands-on controlling role where you can build a broad understanding of our manufacturing operation and have a real impact on how we manage costs, investments and performance.
Your key responsibilities
Business partnering: Act as a financial partner to Plant Management and cost center owners. Provide analysis, challenge assumptions and translate financial performance into clear insights and actions.
Planning & forecasting: Drive key parts of our business planning, budgeting and forecasting processes, including cost centers, Capex, production volumes, headcount and product costs.
Manufacturing performance: Analyze manufacturing costs, productivity and operational deviations. Work with the organization to understand root causes and identify appropriate countermeasures.
Product costing: Lead Planned Product Cost (PPC) calculations, follow Actual Product Costs (APC) and analyze the operational and financial drivers behind deviations.
Investments, assets & inventory: Support investment planning and follow-up, fixed asset management, inventory valuation, physical stocktaking and continuous inventory control.
Reporting & continuous improvement: Drive monthly and annual plant performance reporting while continuously improving our processes, reporting, dashboards and use of SAP and other digital tools.

Qualifications

What distinguishes you
You have a degree in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Industrial Engineering and Management, or a comparable field, together with experience in controlling, financial analysis or a related finance role.
Experience from manufacturing or another industrial environment is particularly valuable.
We are looking for someone with:
Strong analytical skills and confidence working with financial and operational data
Experience with budgeting, forecasting, cost accounting or operational reporting
Good knowledge of Microsoft Excel
Experience working with ERP systems. SAP experience, particularly within controlling or manufacturing processes, is an advantage
Professional working proficiency in English, both written and spoken. Swedish is an advantage, but not a requirement

Experience with product costing, Power BI, automation or other data-analysis tools is an advantage, but you do not need to tick every box. We value your ability to learn, understand the business and turn data into meaningful insights.
Who you are
You are curious about the business behind the numbers. When you see a deviation, your instinct is not simply to report it. You want to understand why it happened, what is driving it and what we can do about it.
You are comfortable asking questions, challenging assumptions and collaborating across functions to find solutions. You can explain financial concepts clearly to colleagues outside Finance and combine strong analytical thinking with a practical mindset.
You take ownership of your work, build strong relationships and are motivated by understanding how a manufacturing business works and how Finance can help make it better.

Additional Information

Why join us in Tranås?
In Tranås, more than 600 associates work across manufacturing and research & development of innovative heating solutions for a more sustainable future.
For a Plant Controller, this creates an exciting environment where you can see the connection between the numbers, the decisions and what actually happens in the factory.
The role gives you broad exposure to manufacturing finance, product costing, investments and operational performance, while working within the international Bosch organization. It is an opportunity to deepen your controlling expertise, influence the business and continue developing your career.
At Bosch, we value openness, trust and different perspectives, and we want our associates to have opportunities to grow both professionally and personally.
What we offer
Competitive compensation
Pension, insurance and other benefits in accordance with our collective agreement
Flexible working hours and hybrid working possibilities where compatible with the role
Employee discounts on Bosch products
Development opportunities within an international Bosch organization

Regular presence at our Tranås site is an important part of the role because of the close collaboration with our manufacturing organization.
If you enjoy combining finance, manufacturing and problem-solving, we would like to hear from you.

Would you like to help develop the next generation of birch forests? Join our research team and investigate how flowering and seed production can support faster progress in forest tree breeding.
Improved planting material contributes to productive and resilient forests. In silver birch, efficient breeding and reliable seed production depend on our ability to understand and influence flowering. Skogforsk is seeking a motivated PhD student to investigate these processes and develop methods that can be applied in breeding programmes and seed production.
The position is part of Phase II of Trees For Me, a centre of excellence focusing on fast-growing broadleaved trees for sustainable forests, materials and energy.

Research project and duties
The overall aim of this four-year PhD project is to improve our understanding of flowering in silver birch and develop practical methods to promote early and reliable flowering and seed production.
The project will investigate how environmental conditions and cultivation treatments influence flowering in young plants and older breeding material. Particular attention will be given to light conditions, plant development and genetic differences in flowering responses. The research will connect fundamental questions about reproductive development with practical challenges in birch breeding.
Earlier flowering could shorten the breeding cycle and help realise the benefits of genomic selection by allowing selected individuals to be crossed at a younger age. Improved control of flowering could also support more reliable seed production.
Your work will include:
Planning, establishing and managing experiments in controlled environments, greenhouses and, where relevant, the field.
Assessing growth, development, male and female flowering, and seed production and quality.
Analysing experimental data using statistical methods.
Publishing scientific papers and communicating results to researchers, breeders and other stakeholders.
Completing doctoral courses in forest genetics, breeding and related subjects.

The detailed research questions and experimental programme will be developed together with the supervisory team.

Trees For Me – Phase II
Trees For Me brings together universities, research institutes, industry and public-sector organisations to develop knowledge and solutions for the sustainable use of fast-growing broadleaved trees, including birch, poplar and aspen.
Within Phase II, this PhD project will contribute knowledge and methods to strengthen birch breeding and the supply of improved reproductive material. The student will participate in an interdisciplinary research environment and collaborate with researchers and stakeholders across the forest sector.

Research environment
The project is a collaboration between Skogforsk and the Southern Swedish Forest Research Centre at the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (SLU) in Alnarp. The student will be employed by Skogforsk and based at the Ekebo research station in Svalöv, with doctoral enrolment at SLU.
You will join a team working with forest tree genetics, breeding and seed production. The position offers close contact with operational breeding, access to experimental facilities and breeding material, and opportunities for national and international collaboration.

Qualifications
We are looking for a motivated and curious candidate with a master’s degree in forestry, biology, plant science, genetics, environmental science or an equivalent subject relevant to the project.
You should have an interest in experimental research, plant development and the practical application of scientific results. Good communication skills and proficiency in spoken and written English are essential.
The following qualifications are considered merits:
Knowledge of plant physiology, flowering biology, forest genetics or tree breeding.
Experience in establishing and managing plant experiments.
Experience in statistical analysis and programming in R or equivalent software.
Experience working with plants in greenhouses, controlled environments or field trials.

You should be able to work independently and collaboratively, organise your work carefully and take responsibility for practical experiments. A valid driving licence is required.
Applicants must meet SLU’s requirements for admission to doctoral studies.

Location: Ekebo research station, Svalöv, Sweden.

Your application should include:

A CV.Degree certificates and transcripts.

Unit for Field-based Forest Research
Would you like to take on a key leadership role, guiding a dedicated team and contributing to the future of field-based forest research? With us, you will have the opportunity to work outdoors in spectacular natural surroundings and help develop groundbreaking projects addressing forest ecosystem and climate-related issues.
We are looking for a hands-on professional with research experience and leadership skills to lead operations at the Siljansfors and Jädraås Experimental Forests, as well as serve as a member of the management team for the entire Unit for Field-Based Forest Research. This position offers excellent opportunities for someone who enjoys a varied range of responsibilities, thrives on challenges, and wants to contribute to research on boreal forest production and forest ecosystems.
In 2024, the Unit revised its strategic operational plan through to 2030, resulting in a partially new organisation structure that has recently been implemented. In line with the Faculty’s ambition to broaden its activities, the Unit’s remit is also being gradually expanded. This calls for a cohesive and functional organisation across the Unit, structured around its four main areas of activity: long-term experiments, major research infrastructure, commissioned projects, and environmental monitoring and analysis.
About the position
You will be a member of the Unit’s management team. As manager of the Siljansfors and Jädraås Experimental Forests, you will have overall responsibility for operations within your area of responsibility (Svealand and southern Norrland), including financial and personnel management, as well as occupational health and safety matters. Your role is to ensure that activities at the experimental forests develop in a way that best supports field research, environmental monitoring, and education, while remaining within the allocated budget. Cooperation within SLU and engagement with the surrounding community are also ongoing aspects of the station managers responsibilities.
As the station manager, you will work together with your colleagues to ensure that ongoing forest field experiments are maintained and revised according to plan, using modern technology, and that new experiments are established today to address future research questions. You will be responsible for the content of metadata databases and the databases associated with them. You will also be responsible for ensuring that the Siljansfors team actively participates in the steering groups for the Unit’s various main areas of activity, and that the tasks agreed upon by these groups are implemented within your area of responsibility. An important part of the role involves receiving requests and, whenever possible, carrying them out. These may concern the establishment or revision of forest field experiments, environmental monitoring assignments, as well as teaching or outreach activities.
During the snow-free season, you will also participate in practical fieldwork, which involves spending considerable time outdoors and undertaking shorter periods of work-related travel.

jobs.description:
Department of Plant Breeding
We are seeking a highly motivated researcher with a strong background in genetics, genomics and crop improvement
About the position
The position focuses on understanding the genetic basis of disease resistance and grain nutrient quality in wheat and lentil, with particular emphasis on micronutrients such as iron and zinc. The overall objective is to identify genetic regions and markers associated with resistance, nutritional and quality traits which can contribute to future breeding efforts. The position will also contribute to the development of data-driven approaches for crop improvement and food innovation. The successful candidate will contribute to integrating advanced genomic and phenotypic approaches with metabolomic and ionomic analyses, food processing and emerging artificial intelligence approaches, within a research environment working at the interface of genetics and pre-breeding/crop improvement.
The candidate will lead experimental and analytical work within the subject and collaborate with other researchers and students in the group as well as outside the organisation.
The work will include:
Analyse Genotyping by sequencing (GBS) data (quality control, read mapping and SNP calling)
Genome-wide association studies (GWAS)
Field evaluation and phenotyping of diverse germplasm
Data analysis, interpretation, and preparation of scientific publications within the subject
Participate in collaborative research activities and supervision of students
Apply for external research funding

Your profile
Qualification requirements
The following qualifications are required:
A PhD in plant genetics, plant breeding, agriculture, or a related field
Good understanding of the genetic basis of complex quantitative traits
Experience with GBS data and GWAS
Experience with nutritional quality traits in crops
Experience with metabolomic and ionomic profiling including the integration and analysis of multi-omics datasets
Experience with advanced statistical methods for analysing genetic and phenotypic data
Practical experience with field experiments, data collection and phenotyping
Good skills in the programming language R or a comparable language
Very good written and oral English skills

The candidate must be able to take a leading role in research development as well as to collaborate in research groups and have good overall communication skills.
Additional qualifications
The following qualifications are meritorious:
Experience in plant pathology and/or plant physiology
Machine learning, artificial intelligence or other data-driven approaches to biological datasets

Assessment criteria
Assessment will be based on the applicant’s scientific competence and experience relevant to the research area of the position. Emphasis will be placed on documented experience in field phenotyping and analysis of genetic data.
The evaluation will also consider the applicant’s ability to conduct independent research, collaborate within a multidisciplinary research environment, and communicate scientific results through publications and presentations.

The Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (SLU) has a key role in the development for sustainable life, based on science and education. Through our focus on the interaction between humans, animals and ecosystems and the responsible use of natural resources, we contribute to sustainable societal development and good living conditions on our planet. Our main campuses are located in Alnarp, Umeå and Uppsala, however, the university also operates at research stations, experimental forests and teaching sites throughout Sweden. SLU has around 4,000 employees, 6,000 students and doctoral students and a turnover of over SEK 4,5 billion. We are investing in attractive environments on all of our campuses. We strive to provide a work environment characterised by inclusivity and gender equality, where different experiences generate conversations between people and pave the way for science, creativity and development. Therefore, we welcome applications from people with diverse backgrounds and perspectives.

Every day, we get opportunities to make a positive impact - on our colleagues, partners, customers, and society. Together, we're pioneering the solutions of the future and unlocking the full potential of precious resources. Trusted to act on initiative, we challenge conventional thinking to develop world-leading technologies that inspire progress in vital areas, including energy, food, water, and shipping. 
As we push forward, the innovative, open spirit that fuels our 140-year-old start-up culture and rapid growth also drives our personal growth. So, as we shape a more resourceful, less wasteful world, we build our careers too. 

About the job 
Ready to take on challenging mechanical engineering work with a clear purpose? 
With us you will contribute to global priorities such as energy efficiency, clean water, and Alfa Laval's net-zero 2030 ambition. Let's shape a better tomorrow together! 
 
We design and supply process solutions within various industries, mainly water treatment. 
As a Mechanical Engineer and FEM/FEA specialist, you will design solutions in 3D with detailed engineering combined with standard components. Our designs contain pipes, pumps, decanters, evaporators, membranes, heat exchangers etc. 
 
Your work involves verification and optimization of mechanical and process equipment, by identifying critical stress concentrations, deformations, and failure modes etc. In this role, you will perform simulations as well as traditional hand calculations to ensure our products meet functional, safety, and regulatory requirements. 
During project execution you will be working in global project teams with Project Managers, Process Specialists, Automation, Sourcing, and Workshops. 
 
Key tasks and responsibilities: 
Design steel structures, skid solutions and custom designs in Autodesk Inventor 
FEM/FEA analysis on mechanical designs using ANSYS/Nastran including: 

Static structural, Buckling, Hydrostatic and internal 
 pressure, Vibrations and fatigue, Thermal and Pipe support. 
Hand calculations 
Prepare clear technical reports and design recommendations 
Review boundary conditions and results from simulations made by others 
Optimize calculation methods, templates, engineering standards, and best practices 
DFM in collaboration with workshop and FAT/SAT 
Review 3D designs and 2D drawings 
Ensure compliance with Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 and CE marking 
Apply relevant standards like ASCE/SEI 7-22 and EN1993-1-1 

 
Planned travels, mostly within Europe, for inspections and commissioning is part of the job - approximately 20 - 25 days per year. 
You will be part of an innovative mechanical team of ten who are continuously implementing smarter ways of working. You report to Jesper Bergstrøm, a people-oriented leader who is passionate about his team thriving in their roles and look forward to going to work. 
At Alfa Laval, we embrace a hybrid work model, allowing you to work from home when it aligns with your tasks. 
 
 
Who are you 
You are a results-driven, high-energy professional who maintains focus and a positive attitude while pursuing ambitious goals. You take initiative, make calculated decisions with confidence, and consistently turn plans into action. You build strong networks across and beyond the organization, using your relational skills to influence, collaborate, and create impact. Proactive, timely, and quality-minded, you work effectively with others and help drive collective success. 
 
What you know 
We are looking for you with solid skills and experience in FEM/FEA analysis with skid- and steel structures solutions. 
The role involves a lot of collaboration and while you can independently, we believe you enjoy collaborating across disciplines and are able to communicate complex technical topics clearly.

Degree in Mechanical Engineering 
Deep knowledge in FEM/FEA analysis with skid- and steel structures solutions. 
Working proficiency in defining the scope, building an efficient model, performing the analysis, interpreting the results, and delivering clear engineering conclusions within a typical timeframe of 1-2 weeks depending on complexity. 
Excellent communication skills in English
